neighbours.label: verbs of physically handling or removing objects (rip out, tear out, haul, move, turn)
fire: You will have to hire someone to tear out the old carpet.
Whether you are ripping out a driveway or a whole patio, call us.
The workers spent the day hauling logs to the river.
The aide moves and arranges furniture and turns mattresses.
He had to drag the heavy boxes up three flights of stairs.
They pulled down the old fence and stacked the boards.
Please lift the crate carefully and set it on the cart.
We shoved the sofa against the wall to make space.
quiet: You will have to hire someone to choose the new colours.
Whether you are planning a driveway or a whole patio, call us.
The workers spent the day talking about the river.
The aide greets visitors and answers the telephone.
He had to explain the plan again to three new members.
They discussed the old fence and agreed on a price.
Please read the label carefully and sign the form.
We admired the sofa in the shop window for a while.

notes: card: weak (max 5.7); hold, tear, rip, haul, move. Opposite pole: complete/finish.
